title: Policies and standards: which few do you need, and does anyone follow them?
short: Keep one signed security policy, an acceptable use page and six topic policies of testable rules, each backed by a setting, and review them yearly.
answer: This quarter, cut your security documents to one management-approved information security policy, an acceptable use page and about six topic policies of short, testable "must" rules, each with an owner and, wherever possible, a setting that enforces it. Review them at least yearly and after significant incidents or changes by checking each rule against the live settings, and keep one mapping table so the same set serves ISO 27001, Grundschutz++ and NIS2 audits.
audience: Heads of security, CISOs and IT leads who write security policies, and the managing directors who approve them, especially under NIS2 or the BSIG

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Keep one short, signed policy on top.
items.text: Two to five pages: scope, objectives, roles, topic policies, approval date. The BSI found more than 20 pages doesn't work in practice[^std2002].

items.title: Cut the rest to about six topic policies.
items.text: ENISA counts ten that 2024/2690 requires of digital providers and accepts one combined document[^enisatig].

items.title: Write rules you can test.
items.text: One sentence per rule, saying who must do what, and one owner per document. Mark advice as advice, as the NCSC asks[^ncscp6].

items.title: Put a setting behind each rule.
items.text: Enforce it in Intune, Group Policy or Conditional Access (Entra ID P1)[^ca]. The CAF rates reliance on users' manual care as not achieved[^caf].

items.title: Review against the settings, not the calendar.
items.text: Each year, compare every rule with a settings export, open exceptions and recent incidents, and log what changed.

blocks.title: Four document levels, and who signs each

items.title: Policy: what and why?
items.text: Intentions and direction formally expressed by management, as ISO/IEC 27002 defines a topic-specific policy[^enisatig]. 2024/2690 has the management body approve the top policy, an appropriate level of management the topic policies[^nis2ir].

items.title: Standard: which settings, exactly?
items.text: Mandatory settings, such as MFA methods, patch deadlines and baselines; NIST calls standards normally compulsory[^sp80012]. Our rule: the heads of security and IT approve them.

items.title: Procedure: which steps?
items.text: Steps for one task, such as creating an admin account[^sp80012]. The process owner approves them; in BSI terms, Arbeitsanweisungen[^std2002].

items.title: Guideline: what do we advise?
items.text: Advice that can be followed in more than one way[^sp80012], published by its author without formal approval.

blocks.title: The documents you actually need
items: **Information security policy.** Approach, objectives, resources, roles, topic policies, records, indicators and approval date, as 2024/2690 lists[^nis2ir]. ENISA maps it to ISO 27001 clause 5.2 and A.5.1[^enisamap].
**Acceptable use.** One or two pages on devices, accounts, data, AI tools and reporting, with the consequences of a breach[^isms1]. Training: the security awareness sheet.
**Access control.** Accounts, MFA, admin accounts, joiners and leavers[^nis2ir].
**Incidents, continuity and backup**[^nis2]; see the incident response, backups and business continuity sheets.
**Suppliers.** Criteria and contract clauses[^nis2ir]; see the third-party risk sheet.
**Data handling and encryption.** Classification, media, disposal, keys[^nis2ir].
**Development, change and testing,** if you build or run software.

blocks.title: Write rules people follow
items: **One rule, one sentence, one "must".** "Admins must sign in with a security key" can be tested; "appropriate authentication" can't. Write advice as "should"[^ncscp6].
**Name the owner, setting and evidence.** The owner keeps the document current[^std2002]; each rule names its setting and the report that proves it.
**Write for the reader.** One page for staff, standards for admins. The CAF rates rules too detailed to remember as not achieved[^caf].
**Ask the people who do the work** whether each rule is usable[^ncscp6].
**In Germany, involve the works council.** It co-determines rules on staff conduct and technical monitoring (BetrVG § 87(1) nos. 1 and 6)[^betrvg].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **German duties apply.** Since 6 December 2025, with no general transition period, the BSI expects processes, responsibilities and measures in writing and reviewed regularly[^bsifaq].

**Grundschutz++ arrived.** BSI-Standard 300-1 (20 October 2026) has management release the policy and requires document control[^std3001]. Certification opens on 1 January 2027; classic IT-Grundschutz stays certifiable until 30 November 2031[^gspp].

blocks.title: Approval and review
items: **NIS2.** Management bodies approve the measures, oversee them and can be held liable[^nis2]; digital providers date the approval in the policy[^nis2ir].
**Germany.** BSIG § 38 has management implement and oversee the § 30 measures, whose compliance must be documented[^bsig]. Minute the approval.
**Topic policies one level down,** by the role the top policy names.
**Yearly and on triggers.** At least annually and after significant incidents or changes[^nis2ir], new laws, audit findings[^enisatig], new technology or an acquisition[^csfie].
**Stagger the rest:** review each yearly[^std2002], two or three a quarter.

blocks.title: Versions, publishing and sign-off
items: **Same header everywhere.** Title, owner, version, last and next review, approval, classification and audience[^std2002], plus a change log.
**One source, one place to read.** A versioned library or Git, one intranet page and old versions archived centrally[^isms1].
**Acknowledge at hire, yearly and on change**[^csfie]. 2024/2690 requires it for the top policy[^nis2ir]; ENISA accepts a digital one or a contract clause[^enisatig].
**Collect it at sign-in.** Entra terms of use (Entra ID P1) can require reacceptance of each version; deleting the terms deletes the records[^entratou].

blocks.title: Exceptions
items: **Write the route into the top policy.** ENISA expects one, with requests, approvals and compensating controls on record and open exceptions reported to management[^enisatig]. Approval levels: the risk register sheet.
**Count them per rule at each review.** A rule that collects exceptions needs rewriting or funding.

blocks.title: One set for several audits
items: **One table, one row per rule:** owner, setting, evidence, ISO 27001 Annex A control, Grundschutz++ or IT-Grundschutz requirement, NIS2 Article 21(2) point, BSIG § 30(2) number.

**Start from official tables.** ENISA maps 2024/2690 to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and CSF 2.0[^enisamap], the BSI § 30 BSIG to ISO 27001[^bsiiso]. A mapping isn't equivalence, ENISA warns[^enisatig]. Certification: the ISMS sheet.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **A template nobody adapted.** It names tools you don't run. SANS's templates, made with CRF[^sanspol], fall under site terms for personal, non-commercial use without changes[^sansterms]; CRF allows internal business use but bars derivative works[^crfterms].
**Settings that contradict the policy.** It demands 90-day password changes, NIST says not to[^sp80063b], and your tenant doesn't.
**Reviews that only change the date.** A new date without a change log shows nobody weighed the incidents and findings.
**A signed policy as the goal.** The BSI asks for proof of effectiveness[^bsicurr].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **A 40-document library.** ENISA accepts the topic policies in one document[^enisatig].
**Signatures on every standard.** Staff acknowledge the top policy and the acceptable use page.
**A policy tool before the first review.** A versioned library and one intranet page will do.
**One set per framework or customer.** Add a mapping column instead.
**Legal prose.** Short sentences hold up better in audits.

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Write the top policy and acceptable use page with your IT provider; the managing director signs.
Adapt CIS's acceptable use template[^cisaup].
Collect acknowledgment at onboarding and yearly.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Keep a top policy, acceptable use and six topic policies with owners, and standards below them.
Collect acknowledgment with Entra terms of use.
Review two or three documents a quarter against settings exports.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Approve one group policy and have each regulated entity's management adopt it with local annexes.
Keep the mapping table in the GRC tool, linked to configuration checks.
Have internal audit test a sample of rules yearly.

changes.text: First draft, based on NIS2, Regulation 2024/2690, ENISA's guidance, the BSIG, BSI ISMS.1, 200-2 and 300-1, NIST CSF 2.0 and the NCSC's CAF.
